title: Emberwake
tagline: What is worth keeping, when you cannot keep everything?

after_the_ember.note: Day 97: after the ending. Lit (the ember in the cradle) or released (spent walking the Choir out), the hand holds no ember: the fog takes nothing, no meter, no pool, the hand's light out (Greying.ember_gone). Lit, the grey goes back everywhere: every Greying area at a third of its strength, look and drain (Greying.after_scale). Dark changes nothing: the ember still walks the Wakebearer through.

act_ends.title: Act I — The Wake
act_ends.subtitle: Saltmarrow remembers you. Mostly.

recap.text: The Gull's Beacon burns on Saltmarrow's lullaby. Nobody there will ever hum it again.
Pell gave the pebble up, and keeps an empty nest clear without knowing why.
The Gull's Beacon burns on the founding knot. Saltmarrow's nets begin in the middle now, and Hesk has stopped humming.
The Gull's Beacon burns on Mara's memory of her brother. She still sets out two cups.
Brother Aldous told you all he could bear to, and cut the ember from his sleeve.
Brother Aldous gave you the bare fact and nothing more.
Mara knows Dunstan walked into the fog by choice.
You carry a message for him: the stool is still by the door.
Oda Farrow remembers a man called Dunstan. The name will not stay with you.
Pell is crossing with you, with Mara's leave, to coil rope on the Slow Mercy.
You promised Pell a crossing, then took it back.
Pell stays on Saltmarrow, and sent a pouch for something lost and good.
Oda Farrow has seen the Keeper's sleeve-ember in your hand.

act_ends.coda: The Slow Mercy sails for Thornwold on the evening tide. Every choice you made here will cross with you.
act_ends.unfinished: Left undone on Saltmarrow for now: %s. The ferry comes back this way.

act_ends.title: Act II — The Drift
act_ends.subtitle: Six lights burn round a dark Spire.

recap.text: The Ridge Light burns on Hob Marl's waiting. He doesn't watch the road for the four any more, and the cold hut is nobody's.
The Ridge Light burns on the salt row. Thornwold's camp will never know who brings its charcoal.
You gave the Lamp its name back: Wynn Sallow.
The Lamp left its name paid in the Book, and stayed the Lamp.
The colliers came up off the far shore with the Lamp's coal for their hearths.
The colliers wait on the Northing's boat-stage for the Spire's boat. You promised to tell the Spire.
The colliers got into Kindleby's skiff, and keep candles on the Keepers' wall now. Ottie looks north from the quay.
The Heron Light burns on Hesper Vail's name. She meets the boats without it.
The Heron Light burns on Corran's knot-cord. Nobody living knows the fen's deep channels.
Dunstan Tollen walked back for his name and rowed home to his stool by Mara's door.
The big man from the rowboat rowed home to Saltmarrow and says he's Mara's brother. She doesn't know him. The second cup is his.
Dunstan Tollen walked back for his name, and stayed on the fen to turn the long walk's boards for whoever comes next.
The big man from the rowboat walked back for his name, and stayed on the fen to turn the long walk's boards.
The Wrack Light burns on Wenna Garrow's answer. Nobody on Wrackholm remembers she ever answered a horn.
The Wrack Light burns on the Gannet's crew board. Her crew are unnamed again on Wrackholm, for good.
The Wrack Light burns on Hale's white-lead pot. Nobody left on Wrackholm has walked the Teeth behind a lampwarden.
You bowed to the Keepers' rite and carried the chapter's choice up the stair.
You told the Provost no, and chose for Kindleby yourself.
The Vigil Light burns on the Boats' Lantern. Nobody on Kindleby remembers how they came over from the Spire.
The Vigil Light burns on Tobin Ashe's coal-pan. He was never called up to the Spire, and will never think to go.
Lowsong's light burns on Iver Lusk's listening. He never heard a voice in the singing, and keeps candles on Kindleby now.
Lowsong's light burns on Iver Lusk's Kindleby. He keeps the rock and listens, and doesn't know there was anywhere else.
Pell sorts Bram's nails at Thornwold's lumber camp.
Pell's lost-things crate has a glass float on top: something lost, something good.
The ember has given back two things of yours: a novice's stair-taper and a bone hood-pin. Someone was counting the landings on the east stair. It was you.
The ember has given back something of yours: a novice's stair-taper, notched for the east stair.

act_ends.coda: The Slow Mercy goes in to Cindermoor on the morning ebb, down a lane no Tidewright has ever sailed. Every light you lit will be burning behind you.
act_ends.unfinished: Still undone on the islands, with a night before the ebb: %s.

act_ends.title: Act III — The Spire
act_ends.subtitle: The hand that carried it down.

recap.text: The Hearthspire burns again. It took the hand that lit it first, and by midwinter it will be hungry. Whoever feeds it now is written down by name, and asked.
The Hearthspire stands dark. The ember walked the Hollow Choir out to the six lights and spent itself, and your hand is only a hand.
The Hearthspire stands dark, and the Choir sings at the top of it. The ember is still in your hand, and at midwinter it goes round the ring.
The Provost would have lit it, and told you so, and left it to you.
The Provost knows whose hand carried the last coal down.
Oriel Sayre came up the east stair behind you, into the room she put out, and signed the Long Book under you.
Oriel Sayre watched it from her boat in the eighth slip, where she always wanted to see the Spire from.
Oriel Sayre counted at the foot, a pace behind the Provost, and signed without being asked.
Your name is back in the seventh place on the novices' roll, in upright Keeper's letters.
Your name is on the roll, struck through. The novice is finished.
The seventh place on the roll stays scraped. Nobody has written you down.
You said Isolde Vane's name up the stair, and she talked to you like a person.
Isolde Vane is in the Long Book as she was: Not Hushed.
Isolde Vane was left to sing, and got the rest of her line out on her own.

act_ends.coda: The Long Book is shut. What the Lanternreach does with its lights now isn't written in any book yet.

act_ends.title: Epilogue — The Lanternreach
act_ends.subtitle: Six weeks to midwinter.

recap.text: The Hearthspire burns gold in the middle of the ring, and every island can see it. The grey has gone back to a third of what it was. Whoever feeds it at midwinter will be written down by name, and asked.
The Hearthspire stands dark, and the six lights burn as if somebody were sitting up with them. Of a morning the step under each one is warm.
The Hearthspire stands dark. At midwinter the ember goes round the ring, and every island chooses its own burning, and writes it down.
Saltmarrow: Mara counts the boats in by the Spire's light, and the green lantern stays on the dock-post.
Saltmarrow: somebody sits up at the Gull's Beacon at night. Tam has taken a blanket up for the step.
Saltmarrow: the village's own list hangs on the dock-post under the green lantern.
The Wrens' brazier burns for the first time since the Snuffing. Aldous feeds it a stick of driftwood a night.
Thornwold: Bram Kettle stopped notching the Spire's row. You don't count a thing that stays.
Under it is a row that's yours, with no notches on it. It isn't for counting.
Thornwold: the night tally at the Ridge Light counts two at the Lamp's bench.
Thornwold: Bram has cut a WINTER row on the tally board. Nobody is to cut a notch on it for anybody else.
Brother Aldous came ashore and climbed to the Ridge Light, and said he was sorry. A door-warden isn't the door. It's a long bench.
Glasswater Fen: the fog lies on the pools thin as breath, and nobody there thanks anybody.
Past the west walk there's a tussock that's yours, to sit by a pool and not be spoken to.
Glasswater Fen: a second light goes round the Heron's walk at night, at the pace the lost keeper used to go.
Glasswater Fen: the list hangs on Hesper's first post, under the gull. The Unmoored are never asked.
Wrackholm: the answering horn answers boats again.
In the lane-house Book, under your own hand: Held for. Whatever the Wakebearer was. A year and a tide.
The Wrack's lantern room is warmest of a morning by the Gannet's empty bracket.
The yard puts things in the iron hand-scale's pan to see what they weigh. Nobody's said they'll give them.
Under the Book's last line, in the same hand: Came in. A fare closed.
Kindleby: the old brothers sit on the quay steps under a gold point in the west, and Tobin is thinking what he'd say.
Kindleby: Tobin changes the candles on the wall so they've got something to sit by.
Kindleby takes the ember first at midwinter. It has waited longest.
At midwinter the ember goes round from the Gull, the way the light goes. Kindleby last.
Lowsong: the Low Water is quiet. The Choir has gone in to the fire.
Brother Iver listens over the Low Water for anything of yours that comes back.
Hild Garrow will row you anywhere the skiff goes, and not ask the Provost.
Lowsong: Iver shares the step under the light with whatever sits there of a morning.
Lowsong: the step under the light is warm of a morning, and it isn't Iver.
Lowsong's list is one name long: Iver's own.
Lowsong's list says: Hild Garrow, for Lowsong, since there's nobody.
The Mercy never put in at Saltmarrow after. Whatever it made of the night, it kept.
The Mercy never put in at Thornwold after. Whatever it made of the night, it kept.
The Mercy never went up the fen's reed channel after. Whatever it made of the night, it kept.
The Mercy never came in past the Teeth after. Whatever Wrackholm made of the night, it kept.
The Mercy never lay under Kindleby's wall after. Whatever it made of the night, it kept.
Nobody rowed you out to Lowsong after. The Low Water kept its own counsel.
You winter on Saltmarrow, where you woke.
You winter at Bram's camp under the black pines.
You winter on the fen, by the pools.
You winter on Wrackholm, within sound of the horn.
You winter on Kindleby, among the candles.
You winter on the Slow Mercy's deck, coiling sun-wise. Oda hasn't let you touch the chart.
You winter on foot, from shingle to shingle. Nobody's counting.

coda.text: The Lanternreach remembers. What it's willing to forget, it will be asked.
Nothing in the Lanternreach burns now that didn't choose to. The lights are kept, and the keepers keep each other.
Nobody chooses for the Lanternreach any more. At midwinter it chooses for itself, and writes it down.

credits: Thank you for carrying it this far.
